lede: Tuesday is the one to watch: a newly seated Town Council takes up second reading of the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, which would write new landscaping and historic-review standards directly into the Land Use Code — that's a real vote on rules that affect properties across town. Same day, the Telluride Housing Authority meets to work out a primary-residency policy for dependents in multi-custodial households, a question with direct consequences for families trying to qualify for deed-restricted housing. Thursday, Planning and Zoning digs into three Town-owned development projects in the Accommodations 2 zone, including the Carhenge redevelopment at 700 W Pacific.

notable.stake: Second-reading vote on wildfire code changes to Land Use Code landscaping and historic review.
New primary-residency policy for dependents could affect deed-restricted housing eligibility.
P&Z reviews subdivision and concept plans for three Town-owned Accommodations 2 zone projects.
